candidates.name: Pleural effusion
support_spans: complete opacification of the left hemithorax with tracheal shift to the right, consistent with massive left pleural effusion
large left pleural effusion with passive basal lung collapse
candidates.why: The patient presents with progressive dyspnea and chest pain, and imaging studies confirm a large left pleural effusion.

candidates.name: Pancreatic pseudocyst
support_spans: multiple non-enhancing cystic areas in the pancreas
small intrapancreatic collection at the tail
candidates.why: The patient has a history of acute severe pancreatitis and imaging studies show cystic areas in the pancreas.

candidates.name: Pancreaticopleural fistula
support_spans: amylase 11,871 U/L in pleural fluid
history of acute severe pancreatitis
candidates.why: The high amylase level in the pleural fluid suggests a connection between the pancreas and the pleural space.

candidates.name: Chylothorax
support_spans: dark brown, turbid fluid on thoracentesis
candidates.why: The appearance of the pleural fluid is consistent with chylothorax, which can occur due to a fistula or other conditions.

candidates.name: Empyema
support_spans: culture negative
MTB/RIF PCR negative
candidates.why: The negative culture and PCR results make empyema less likely, but the high LDH and protein levels in the pleural fluid could still suggest an infectious or inflammatory process.

candidates.name: Malignant pleural effusion
support_spans: no malignant cells on cytology
candidates.why: The absence of malignant cells on cytology makes malignant pleural effusion less likely, but further testing may be needed to rule it out.
